near_miss.why_not: Only shared items are 'woman' and a 'sit' verb in unrelated settings (seating by lot at a feast vs widow remaining in the household, a legal idiom); no shared phrase.

near_miss.lead: ON (arrow) fló ... meðal ... rifja ~ byliny бьет коня по крутым ребрам
near_miss.why_not: Cognate rif ~ ребро but different action (arrow flying between a man's ribs vs whipping a horse's flanks); body-part noun with a locative is everyday language.

near_miss.lead: ON bitu ... vápn (weapons bite) ~ Skt bhittvā vyūham
near_miss.why_not: bíta 'bite (of weapons)' vs bhid 'split (an array)': different objects and syntax; no shared collocation.

near_miss.lead: *mergʷ- 'dark' + *nókʷts 'night': ON myrkt (af) nótt ~ Serbian мркла ноћ / ноћи мрака
near_miss.why_not: Cognates real (ON myrkr ~ Sl. *mьrkъ/mrakъ), but 'dark night' is a universal pairing. collocates_8c pair search: Germanic hits are all ON saga prose (a 13th-c.+ cliché 'gerði myrkt af nótt'); none in Edda or OE (Edda 'Myrkt es úti' has no 'night'; OE myrce goes with mōr); Slavic only these two Vuk lines, nothing in ORu or byliny (which use тьма/темная). Late on both sides, generic.

near_miss.lead: ON Hljóðs biðjum (poet asks a hearing, *ḱlew-) ~ ORu оухо слыша
near_miss.why_not: The Russian is the 1 Cor 2:9 quotation (eye has not seen, ear has not heard): biblical, not a request for a hearing. Better partner is outside the slab (see search lead).

near_miss.lead: *webʰ- 'weave' figure: ON vefr darraðar (battle as a web of spears, Hǫfuðlausn) ~ Gk μῆτιν ὕφαινον
near_miss.why_not: Cognate verb/noun, but the object differs (battle vs counsel); the weaving metaphor for planning is cross-culturally common and ON vefr darraðar has its own ON/OE background (darraðr from OE daroþ). Not the same figure.

near_miss.lead: *h₂eḱ- + *h₂egʷsih₂: ON eggju ... øxi ~ Gk ὀξέσι πελέκεσσι καὶ ἀξίνῃσι
near_miss.why_not: In Greek ὀξέσι goes with πελέκεσσι, not ἀξίνῃσι; in ON egg and øx sit in separate clauses of the helmingr. Pair search: 4 ON prose hits (axe-edge as an object noun), 1 Greek: generic weapon vocabulary.

near_miss.lead: water + fish: ON hvert vatn uddi af fiskum ~ MIr (cona tibridis) usce a iasc
near_miss.why_not: Cognates iasc ~ fiskr, uisce ~ vatn (same root, different formation). But the Irish belongs to the motif of a wronged/fasting party's curse on fertility (water its fish, wood its mast, earth its fruit), while the ON is a settler's description of plentiful fishing. Different context; water–fish is a natural pairing.

search_lead.cognate: ON hljóð n. 'hearing, silence' < PGmc *hleuþa- < *ḱléw-tom (cf. Ved. śrótra-, Av. sraoθra-); Av. sraotā imperative of *ḱlew- 'hear'
search_lead.argument: Both are a poet's opening call for a hearing before a solemn recitation (Egill's Hǫfuðlausn: Hljóðs biðjum hann; Vǫluspá 1: Hljóðs bið ek allar kindir; Gāthā Y 45.1: āt̰ frauuaxšiiā nū gūšōdūm nū sraōtā, followed by 'you who come from near and far'), with *ḱlew- carrying the request in both. In ON it is a noun object of biðja and in Avestan a verb, so the shape has been renewed. The ON saga idiom kveðja sér hljóðs (an assembly speaker asking for a hearing) shows the phrase was also everyday, which weakens it. I recall West (IEPM) listing the poet's request for attention across traditions.
